delivery.rule: notices shown in a brief are marked delivered to that agent so a second brief on the same paths does not repeat them; delivery is NOT an ack, acked_by is untouched and notice_ack stays explicit
delivery.scope: delivered marks are per daemon lifetime, held in State, never written to notices.jsonl (a rewrite of the log on every claim would undo ADR-0010); after a daemon restart a notice may be briefed once more, which is harmless
delivery.unread_for_lists: notice_list unread:true is unchanged and still lists delivered-but-unacked notices

shape.ids: 8-char prefixes are accepted by notice_ack, contract_get and decision-related inputs per task 89b35cb6 (storage-claude); brief depends on that landing first

input.semantics: when true, the ok response carries the brief sections below for the claimed paths only; brief:false returns the bare claim outcome (no notices/contracts/decisions/memory sections). No new tool, no new schema entry beyond one boolean.

shape.ordering: every section newest first by its published_at / recorded_at / updated_at

output.contracts: newest 5 contracts consumed by the claimed paths: [{name, version, kind}]; fetch bodies with contract_get
output.decisions: newest 5 decisions affecting the claimed paths: [{id: 8-char prefix, title}]
output.existing_fields: claim_id, new_paths, renewed_paths, expires_at stay exactly as today
output.memory: unchanged from contract "Memory primitive" v3: at most 5 newest notes, [{permalink, title, kind, paths, updated_at, excerpt<=160}], never a body; brief:false suppresses it like the other sections
output.more: {notices: n, contracts: n, decisions: n, memory: n} = how many matching rows were NOT shown; always present when brief is on so the agent knows whether to page with the list tools
output.notices: newest 5 unread-and-undelivered notices overlapping the claimed paths: [{id: 8-char prefix, kind, summary (<=160 chars, truncated with an ellipsis), by}]
output.omitted_when_empty: each of notices/contracts/decisions/memory is absent (not []) when it has no rows; more is still present
output.size: hard cap 4096 bytes for the serialized ok response. Enforced after rendering: while over the cap, drop the oldest row from the largest section and bump its `more` count. tests/http_roundtrip.rs asserts the cap with 40 max-length notices, 20 contracts, 40 decisions and 20 notes on one path.
output.where: only on status ok; conflict responses are unchanged

shape.protocol_after: claim (brief on) -> edit -> notice_publish on breaking changes -> release. notice_list / contract_list / decision_list / memory_search remain for paging when `more` says there is more, and for paths you are not claiming.
shape.task_pull: out of scope for v1 of this contract; a follow-up may attach the same brief for a pulled task's paths

current.notes: v1, designed 2026-09-16 by claude-token-diet for task 87e14abd. Purpose: replace the four reads the dogfooding protocol requires before every edit (notice_list, contract_list, decision_list, memory_search) with one claim response, cutting a work cycle from 7 round trips to 4 (measured on the swarm bench: 7.0 calls and ~2,350 shipped tokens per claim->release cycle with synthetic bodies; ~13k tokens per cycle against this repo's real state). Row shapes follow the compact-row direction of task 89b35cb6 (8-char ids, no nulls, no empty arrays) and reuse the Memory primitive v3 claim row unchanged. Default true because an opt-in flag is the step agents forget; brief:false exists for renew-style re-claims and for clients that render claims themselves. Implementation waits for src/server.rs and src/state.rs to be released in the agreed order (memory-layer, ci-speedup, storage-claude, then me). ADR: docs/5-decisions/0014-brief-on-claim.md.
